validity.researcher_notes: This is a well-documented, real, formally authorized and formally terminated PNGRB common-carrier pipeline -- not a phantom/GEM-only entity. Starting from the sheet's own wiki citations: two of the four cited URLs (PNGRB EOI-archive PDF and PNGRB Grant-of-Authorization PDF) are dead/rotted (one 404s, the other 200s but no longer contains 'Surat'/'Paradip' -- PNGRB appears to have reorganized its PDF archive), so they cannot be cited, but the other two -- LiveMint and Economic Times, both contemporaneous March 2018 news reports -- verify live and are fully independent of each other and of GEM. Both confirm: GAIL (India) Ltd was awarded the licence in April 2012 (Bid No. BID/NGPL/03/2010/1/SPPL, GAIL having bid an unusually low Rs0.01/mmBtu tariff in Nov 2011, beating GSPC India Transco); GAIL then made zero ground progress for six years; PNGRB penalised GAIL in Sept 2015 (encashing 25% of its Rs20cr performance bank guarantee), GAIL's court challenge was dismissed by the Delhi High Court in April 2017, and after further warnings (18 Jan 2018 and 20 Feb 2018 PNGRB letters, per ET) PNGRB terminated the authorisation entirely by a 13 March 2018 order (encashing the remaining guarantee) -- reported by both outlets on 14-15 March 2018. This is a CONFIRMED cancellation (a regulator formally terminating an authorisation), matching the sheet's existing ShelvedCancelledType=confirmed exactly -- correct as recorded, not one of the 8 blank rows in this cluster. Classification as transmission gas pipeline is correct: this was described by both sources as 'the country's first pipeline originating and terminating at a port' and was authorized under PNGRB's Natural Gas Pipeline (NGPL) common-carrier framework, which covers inter-state transmission trunk lines, not gathering/distribution/CGD networks. No duplicate risk against the roster: Surat (Gujarat) to Paradip (Odisha) is a distinct west-to-east coastal corridor that does not geographically overlap any of the other 12 in-scope rows (the Rajasthan/Langtala cluster, the West Bengal cluster, the Andhra cluster, or P0451 Iran-Pakistan-India). Owner attribution (GAIL India Ltd, 100%) is explicitly confirmed by both articles. Tried to also verify ProposalYear: a web-search summary of a PNGRB bid-round document suggested a public notice dated 25.11.2010 for this bid, but I could not independently verify that specific PDF (the PNGRB bid-archive PDF I checked at a plausible URL loaded fine but did not mention Surat/Paradip), so I am not fabricating a ProposalYear fill off an unverified secondary summary -- left blank for a future pass with better PNGRB-archive access.

fills.researcher_notes: PNGRB terminated GAIL's authorisation by a 13 March 2018 order, reported by both outlets 14-15 March 2018. Two independent contemporaneous news sources.
Both sources explicitly call it a 'natural gas pipeline'; ET's headline names it directly.

No source uses the literal word 'transmission', but LiveMint describes a 2,112-km inter-state trunk line authorized under PNGRB's common-carrier Natural Gas Pipeline (NGPL) regime -- the country's first port-to-port pipeline -- unambiguously transmission-class, not gathering/distribution/CGD. Classification correct.

PNGRB's termination order is dated 13 March 2018 (LiveMint: 'according to the regulator's 13 March order'); ET independently corroborates the same week's events (18 Jan and 20 Feb 2018 warning letters, then a 'Tuesday order' terminating the licence, published 14 Mar 2018). Both agree the cancellation occurred in 2018.

LiveMint states design capacity of 74.81 million standard cubic meters per day (MMSCMD). Converted: 74.81 MMSCMD x 365 days = ~27.31 bcm/y, matching GEM's 27.30 bcm/y within normal day-count rounding. Only one source states the exact figure (the PNGRB primary documents that would corroborate it are dead links), so tier=medium rather than high.

LiveMint states '2,112-km long pipeline' verbatim, an exact match to GEM's LengthKnown=2112.00 km. Only one live source states this exact figure (the two PNGRB primary documents that would corroborate it are dead links), so tier=medium rather than high; a low-quality web-search summary of a bid-round PDF mentioned a conflicting '1500 km', but I could not verify that PDF's actual content (it 200s but does not mention Surat/Paradip), so I disregard it rather than let an unverifiable snippet override a verified, on-point news source.

LiveMint: 'a natural gas pipeline from Surat in Gujarat to Paradip in Odisha'. ET independently names the same route in its headline and body. Both endpoints and both states confirmed by 2 independent sources.

Both sources name GAIL (India) Ltd as the sole licence-holder/sponsor of this pipeline throughout its authorization-to-cancellation history (awarded 2012, penalised 2015, litigated 2017, terminated 2018). No co-sponsor is ever mentioned -- 100% ownership by GAIL confirmed.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: This is not a dormancy inference -- it is a CONFIRMED regulatory cancellation. PNGRB formally terminated GAIL's authorisation for the Surat-Paradip pipeline by a 13 March 2018 order (encashing the remaining Rs15cr performance bank guarantee), after GAIL made zero ground progress for six years following its April 2012 authorisation, was penalised in Sept 2015, lost a Delhi High Court challenge in April 2017, and failed to meet a Jan/Feb 2018 final-warning deadline. Two independent contemporaneous news sources (LiveMint, Economic Times) agree on every material fact and date. Searched for any post-2018 news of revival, re-bid, or successor project on this exact Surat-Odisha corridor and found none among the sheet's own wiki citations or in general search; no evidence GAIL or any other sponsor has since resumed or re-tendered this specific route. Status=cancelled and the sheet's existing ShelvedCancelledType=confirmed are both correct as recorded -- no change needed. CancelledYear=2018 matches the order date exactly.

summary: P0955 (Surat-Paradip Gas Pipeline) is a real, extensively documented PNGRB-authorized pipeline -- confirmed cancelled/2018 (PNGRB terminated GAIL's licence for zero progress after 6 years) via 2 independent contemporaneous news sources; Status/ShelvedCancelledType=confirmed/CancelledYear/Fuel/PipelineType/Owner/Length(2112km)/Capacity(27.30 bcm/y)/Location all now sourced, no existence/duplicate/classification/attribution concerns found; only gap is ProposalYear, left blank for lack of a verifiable primary source.
